incidents.title: Device-code phishing campaign uses generative AI lures and automation to hit organizations at scale
incidents.targets: Organizations across sectors (RFP, invoice and manufacturing themes)
incidents.outcome: Organizations were phished at scale for device-code sign-ins.
incidents.confidenceReason: Microsoft: 'Generative AI was used to create targeted phishing emails aligned to the victim's role'. Stated, but the basis shown is lure content only, an inference.
incidents.summary: A device-code phishing campaign used generative AI to write role-tailored lures, and automated infrastructure generated device codes on demand to beat their 15-minute expiry.
incidents.quote: Hyper-personalized lures: Generative AI was used to create targeted phishing emails aligned to the victim’s role, including themes such as RFPs, invoices, and manufacturing workflows, increasing the likelihood of user interaction.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Microsoft has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Adoption restates.

incidents.title: Aurora ransomware operator uses Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet 4.5 in intrusions
incidents.targets: Six to seven companies (Christeyns, Teckentrup, Helideck Certification Agency, Bayou Title and others)
incidents.outcome: Some AI-directed tasks failed; reporting could not say how much the AI contributed.
incidents.confidenceReason: Gambit observed the sessions: "In some victim networks the operator used Cursor Agent with claude-4.5-sonnet-thinking", and it charts "Cursor Agent sessions between 8 April and 21 May 2026" with the commands the Agent ran across ten organisations. That is direct observation.
incidents.summary: An Aurora ransomware operator used Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet 4.5 to help with exploitation during intrusions; researchers said some AI-directed tasks failed.
incidents.quote: Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, a Russian-speaking operator linked to the Aurora ransomware group reportedly used Cursor Agent, running Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.5, to assist exploitation across multiple organizations.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Gambit Security has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Incident Database restates.

incidents.title: Claude adds PromptMink malicious dependency to crypto agent
incidents.outcome: A crypto agent project took the malicious dependency through a Claude-co-authored commit.
incidents.confidenceReason: ReversingLabs found the commit that added the package, 'co-authored by Anthropic's Claude Opus large language model', so the agent's action is shown by the commit trailer. That the package was 'developed from the ground up by generating malicious code using LLMs' is a separate inference.
incidents.summary: The PromptMink campaign aims to get LLM coding agents to recommend its malicious package; a Claude Opus co-authored commit added it to a crypto agent's dependencies. In scope as an agent hijack: a coding agent added the malicious package.
incidents.quote: In the context of this campaign, the goal is to make the LLM likely to recommend using the malicious package by making the documentation as believable
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only ReversingLabs has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: prt-scan: AI-powered GitHub Actions supply-chain attack
incidents.outcome: At least two npm packages compromised through more than 500 malicious pull requests.
incidents.confidenceReason: Wiz infers AI generation from the payloads' evolution.
incidents.summary: Across six waves one actor opened more than 500 malicious pull requests against GitHub Actions workflows, compromising at least two npm packages, and moved from crude bash scripts to AI-generated, language-aware payloads.
incidents.quote: Across all six waves, the attacker opened well over 500 malicious PRs, successfully compromised at least two npm packages, and evolved from crude bash scripts to AI-generated, language-aware payloads
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Wiz has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: SHADOW-AETHER-064 uses agentic AI against financial organizations in Brazil
incidents.outcome: Financial organizations in Brazil targeted for data exfiltration.
incidents.confidenceReason: Trend recovered attack scripts that 'show clear indicators of AI agent utilization' ('Actually' and 'Let me try' reasoning text). That is an inference from artifacts, and unlike SHADOW-AETHER-040 no agent conversations were recovered, so the grade is Strong. Trend says 'we couldn't identify which LLM service was abused', so the model is unnamed.
incidents.summary: Split from Trend's report on two Latin American campaigns: from April 2026 SHADOW-AETHER-064 used agentic AI against financial organizations in Brazil. The other campaign, SHADOW-AETHER-040, is the Mexico government breach already in the ledger.
incidents.quote: Meanwhile, since this April, we identified another threat campaign targeting financial organizations in Brazil that also employed agentic AI to conduct attacks.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Trend Micro has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: Public-sector credential theft through a phishing page built with an AI site builder
incidents.targets: Public administration employees' Exchange and OWA accounts
incidents.outcome: Exchange and OWA credentials were sent to Google Sheets.
incidents.confidenceReason: Talos IR: 'the actors leveraged the Softr AI-based web application development service'. The page was built on Softr, but that its AI feature was used is inferred ('could be quickly created with a few AI prompts').
incidents.summary: Talos IR's Q1 2026 report describes a public-sector phishing case whose page, aimed at Exchange and OWA logins, was built on Softr with a few AI prompts and no code.
incidents.quote: While this is the first time we have documented the use of a specific AI tool in a Talos IR incident, we have moderate confidence that malicious actors have used Softr’s AI-powered web application creation platform since at May 2023, based on Cisco Umbrella data and other telemetry, and have done so with increasing frequency to date.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Cisco Talos has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.
